problem.statement: Allow a browser to send credentialed cross-origin requests (cookies or Authorization headers) by responding with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.

approach.summary: Set Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and expect credentialed fetch/XHR requests to succeed.

failure.point: The Fetch standard forbids the wildcard origin for credentialed requests; the browser blocks the response unless the server echoes the specific request Origin and sends Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.
failure.evidence: The WHATWG Fetch specification (CORS protocol) and MDN document that "*" is invalid with credentials; the server must reflect the exact Origin and set Allow-Credentials: true.

environment.description: Evergreen browsers enforcing the Fetch/CORS protocol.

transferability.notes: Enforced by browsers, not by the server or non-browser clients (curl, server-to-server). Non-credentialed requests may use "*" freely.
